transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-22
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Li (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Nexis ML Lead), Priya Varma (Nexis Infra), Sam O'Neil (Nexis DS)

Summary:
- Diego walked through sensitivity heatmap results for INT8 and FP8 variants; main regressions concentrated on long-form summarization prompts and a small subset of entity-heavy prompts.
- Throughput/latency dives showed ~2.4x token/sec improvement at batch=4 for INT8 on A100-like instance but tail latency increased slightly on cold KV cache misses.
- Agreement on next steps: focused 1k evaluation, representative prompt set from Nexis, updated pricing for dedicated burst.

Topics:
- Sensitivity heatmap interpretation
- Throughput deltas (batching, cache warm/cold)
- Regression triage and rollback/fallback policies
- Enterprise constraints: VPC, KMS, SOC2 audit expectations

Action items recap (explicit): see metadata action_items field

Transcript body:
[00:00] Morgan: Okay everyone on the line? Good afternoon Alex, Priya, Sam. We have Diego and I from Redwood. Quick agenda walk: heatmap review, throughput numbers, then triage plan.
[00:18] Alex: Sounds good. We saw the slide deck you sent, thanks. We're most worried about the summarization regressions — those hit customer-facing emails.
[00:28] Diego: Yeah, so we ran the sensitivity sweep across INT8, FP8, and a mixed precision blend. The heatmap highlights delta in SNR and the fraction of outputs that failed the entity check. Important note, some of the labels are noisy — the auto-diff tooling mis-labeled a few s.. s.. samples.
[00:47] Sam: When you say "entity check" can you restate the metric? Is that exact span matching or fuzzy match?
[00:52] Diego: It's a fuzzy-span match with a 0.6 threshold, so it's forgiving. That said the regressions were concentrated where the prompt included many short entities in colloquial forms — bank account references, transaction ids, etc.
[01:09] Priya: Are those the same prompts that we've been using in the earlier weekly? I noticed some overlap but not exact.
[01:14] Morgan: Good call. Alex you mentioned you'd curate a canonical set — that'll help. Also Diego, can you show the heatmap again?
[01:21] Diego: Yep, screen share. So here's the heatmap: rows are prompt buckets, columns are model variants — baseline FP16, FP8, INT8, and blended INT8-with-KV-cache-warming. The darker red means more quality delta from baseline.
[01:38] Diego: The big cluster is long-form summarization (>300 tokens) and a small island at entity-heavy transactional prompts. FP8 does better than INT8 on the long-form, INT8 gains on throughput but loses fidelity on entity spans.
[01:53] Alex: Can you quantify "does better" — what's the SNR delta?
[01:57] Diego: Median SNR delta FP8 vs FP16 is ~0.8 dB on our test set, INT8 is about -2.1 dB compared to FP16 for the same prompts. For the entity-span F1 metric, FP8 drops 1-2%, INT8 drops 6-9% in the worst buckets.
[02:19] Sam: That's bigger than we feared on entity stuff. Is that uniform across sequence length?
[02:24] Diego: It's correlated: shorter sequences with many entities are hit harder — probably an embedding quantization effect.
[02:31] Morgan: How about latency/throughput? You had numbers for batch sizes?
[02:35] Diego: Yes. On our dedicated A100-like test instance we measured tokens/sec at batch sizes 1, 4, 8. INT8 at batch=4 gives ~2.4x tokens/sec vs FP16 baseline. FP8 gives ~1.6x. Tail latency for INT8 p95 increased by ~18% in cold-cache scenarios. Warm cache tail latency was fine.
[02:58] Priya: Cold K V cache misses — is that the KV load from new conversations or full model hotstart?
[03:05] Diego: Mostly KV cache warm-up when the sequence is longer — the runtime needs to allocate and populate KV entries. There's also a slight kernel scheduling jitter on the INT8 path when memory bandwidth spikes.
[03:21] Priya: Any mitigations? We can't have p95 jump in production for onboarding user flows.
[03:26] Diego: We have two pragmatic levers: pre-warming (keep a small warm pool for expected session patterns) and hybrid routing — route onboarding flows to FP8 or baseline until cache warms, then switch to INT8. The runtime supports transparent fallback policies.
[03:41] Alex: How invasive is hybrid routing? Will it require code changes on our side?
[03:45] Morgan: No code changes typically. It's a routing policy in the deployment config; we can set sticky routing rules based on session id or route key.
[03:54] Sam: For the regression triage — can we get a per-prompt diff so we can see exact tokens differences?
[03:59] Diego: Yes, we'll produce diffs for the top 200 failing prompts. In this week we focused on aggregated metrics but we can push per-sample diffs.
[04:08] Alex: Great. Also are there any known issues with our on-prem env? We're considering Redwood Private later.
[04:13] Diego: The characteristics should be similar, but the kernel mix depends on the GPU. We tested on A100, on V100 the INT8 perf delta is smaller; on H100 INT8 and FP8 both look strong. For Private deployments, we provide a compatibility matrix.
[04:29] Priya: Security question — KMS and logs. Will the fallback routing leak any PII into logs? We need to keep audit trail minimal.
[04:36] Morgan: We redact PII at the tokenization boundary, and audit logs record only metadata — route id, model variant, latency — not full prompts unless you enable debug logging. We also integrate with your KMS for model keys and with HSM for rotation if needed.
[04:52] Alex: Ok good. Back to the heatmap — is there a threshold where we mark a prompt bucket as "no-go" for INT8?
[04:58] Diego: We propose a policy based on delta F1 and business impact. For buckets where entity F1 drops >5% and business-critical label=high, we mark as "no-go" and route those to FP8/baseline. We can auto-generate a blocking list from the canonical prompt set.
[05:16] Sam: What about mixed precision? You mentioned a blend earlier.
[05:19] Diego: Right — mixed precision blends INT8 for the bulk of tokens and FP8 for the last N tokens or for attention layers sensitive to precision. That reduced the entity F1 loss by half while preserving ~1.8x throughput. It's a middle ground.
[05:36] Alex: And implementation complexity?
[05:38] Diego: It's a runtime config; the model variant is a single artifact with a micro-kernel switch. No retraining required.
[05:44] Priya: For SLA planning, can you give a sense of unit cost delta if we go INT8 blended?
[05:50] Morgan: We'll send a pricing note but rough order: INT8 pure reduces token compute cost by ~40-55% depending on GPU and batch sizing; blended INT8->FP8 net is ~30% savings. Dedicated reserved capacity reduces billing variance further.
[06:03] Alex: Okay. One more thing — hallucination: did you see increases?
[06:07] Diego: Hallucination rate increased modestly in INT8 for long-form summarization — about a 1.5% absolute increase on our hallucination detector. FP8 had near-zero delta.
[06:18] Sam: For our product, hallucination >2% is a red flag. So we need to keep total under that.
[06:24] Diego: Agreed, that's why blended mode might be the best short-term approach.
[06:30] Morgan: Let's talk about the focused 1k eval. Diego, what's your plan and timeline?
[06:34] Diego: We'll select 1k canonical prompts from the set Alex will provide, stratified by bucket: long-form, entity-heavy, short queries. We'll run FP16 baseline, FP8, INT8, and mixed-blend. We'll output per-sample diffs, SNR, entity F1, hallucination flags, and latency distributions — warm vs cold cache. Expect results in 4 business days.
[06:56] Alex: That timeline works. Priya will hand over infra logs and stored traces for the last 2 weeks for noise analysis.
[07:03] Priya: Yep, we'll share an anonymized bundle.
[07:06] Diego: For the test harness, one caveat: our auto-detect of entity spans uses a brittle ner model; some spans were missed in noisy user text causing inflated deltas. We'll run a secondary spaCy-based check to reduce false positives.
[07:20] Sam: Good call.
[07:23] Morgan: Any blockers from Nexis side to run the pilot further?
[07:26] Alex: Only the canonical prompts, which we'll assemble. Also we want a separate benchmark on evening peak hours — can you emulate 1.2x concurrency loads?
[07:34] Diego: Yes, we can run a synthetic concurrency sweep to emulate your peak hours; we'll include a 1.2x and 1.5x scenario.
[07:42] Priya: One infra question — persistent KV cache persistence across restarts: do you persist between container restarts or it's ephemeral?
[07:49] Diego: Currently ephemeral to keep memory semantics simple. We can implement a small checkpointing flow but it adds complexity. For most applications, keeping a warm pool is sufficient.
[07:58] Priya: Hmm we might need checkpointing for rapid cold starts in our on-prem case. Could you add an estimate for engineering effort?
[08:05] Diego: We'll estimate in the follow-up; rough ballpark 2-3 sprint-weeks of effort to add a persistent KV snapshot/restore mechanism across our runtime.
[08:15] Alex: Noted.
[08:18] Morgan: Quick competitor note — we've seen other vendors push quantized models but without routing and fallback, customers see regressions. Our differentiator is the rollout policies and per-route SLOs.
[08:30] Alex: Makes sense.
[08:32] Sam: Can we talk about the visualization you used — the heatmap colors were somewhat hard to read for color-blind folks. Any alternative outputs?
[08:40] Diego: Absolutely — we'll add numerics and a sorted table, and produce a CSV so you can filter. Also add a delta-sorted listing.
[08:48] Priya: For auditability, can we store the diffs in S3 with per-sample checksum?
[08:53] Diego: Yes, we'll push artifacts to a signed S3 URL you control or to an internal artifact store with access controls.
[08:59] Alex: Awesome.
[09:01] Morgan: We're coming up on the 10 minute mark? Wait, oh the call duration is 48, so we've got time.
[09:08] Diego: One more thing — fallback rules: we recommend a conservative config for your first rollout: block any bucket with entity F1 drop >5% and route to FP8; enable blended for long-form; pre-warm pool size 10 for onboarding routes.
[09:26] Alex: Works for us. How do we toggle those in Console?
[09:30] Morgan: It's a routing policy JSON; we can commit a canary that applies to 10% of traffic then ramp. Diego will provide a sample policy.
[09:38] Diego: I'll attach an example with param comments.
[09:41] Priya: Regarding compliance, SOC2 — do you retain audit logs per user? We need retention 1 year.
[09:47] Morgan: Yes, enterprise plan offers configurable retention up to multi-year; we can scope export and storage to your S3.
[09:54] Alex: Any final questions?
[09:57] Sam: No, this was good. Quick request — can we get a small matrix showing where INT8 is safe vs where blended is better?
[10:04] Diego: Yes, that will be part of the 1k evaluation deliverable: a per-bucket recommendation (INT8 | FP8 | Blend).
[10:11] Morgan: Recap of next steps: Diego runs 1k eval, Morgan sends pricing, Alex provides prompts, Priya shares logs. We'll reconvene after Diego posts the artifact.
[10:24] Alex: Great, thanks everyone.
[10:27] Morgan: Thanks, talk soon.
[10:30] (call ends)

Post-call notes:
- Diego to include both per-sample diffs and an aggregated csv with columns: prompt_id, bucket, baseline_score, fp8_score, int8_score, blend_score, hallucination_flag, entity_f1, latency_warm_ms, latency_cold_ms.
- Morgan will include a simple sample routing policy for canary gating in the follow-up email.
- Customer will prioritize the 50 most important prompts and hand them over by Monday.

Transcript end.
